title: Honing and polishing sequence for natural stone and terrazzo
audience: Stone and terrazzo restoration technicians who run honing and polishing machines on natural stone and terrazzo
learningOutcomes: Explain why honing comes before polishing and why each grit must remove the scratches of the previous one
Keep the wet method running throughout each honing and polishing step
Inspect a finished surface for scratches, pits, colour change, edge damage and loosening chips
Record the grit sequence, the water and extraction checks and the inspection result
referencesAtStart: Official sources for this lesson: NT WorkSafe, Guide to working with crystalline silica and crystalline silica containing products (version 1.1, 29 January 2026); Safe Work Australia, Working with silica and silica containing products (national guidance) (February 2022).

instruction.heading: Plan the sequence before the first pass
instruction.body: Honing removes marks, levels the surface and opens the stone to the next step. Polishing uses finer abrasives to build the sheen. The two stages run in order, and each stage has to remove the scratch pattern of the one before it. The grit numbers, the pad types, the machine speeds and the number of passes are set by the product or the manufacturer's instructions for the material. This course does not give a national grit sequence or machine speed, because no Australian standard for natural stone restoration method was found and the sequence depends on the stone. Use the sequence confirmed by the test patch in “Pre-work surface assessment and test patches”, and write it on the job record before the first pass.

instruction.heading: Keep the wet method running through every step
instruction.body: The wet method is the main dust control for honing and polishing, and it applies at every grit. Start the water before the machine starts, and keep the flow at the point of cut for the whole pass. Check the flow when you change the grit or pad and at regular intervals. Keep the pads clean and free of debris, because a loaded pad scratches the surface and can heat up. Dry honing and dry polishing are stop-work matters under “Respirable crystalline silica: where it comes from and why it matters” and are not permitted in this course. The NT WorkSafe guide describes dry cutting, grinding or polishing without controls as generating very high silica levels. Where the slurry becomes thick and dry at the edges, stop, restore the flow and clean the edges with the wet method before continuing.

instruction.heading: Check the result before you call it finished
instruction.body: Inspect the surface under good light and from the angles at which the client will see it. Look for remaining scratches from the coarser grit, pits, colour change, uneven sheen and edge damage. On terrazzo, check each chip for looseness and stop before the grinding exposes or lifts the aggregate. Over-grinding terrazzo changes the look and can loosen the chips, so stop at the point where the matrix and chips are level and the surface is even. If the surface shows damage, stop and refer it, and record the damage in the job record. When the inspection passes, record the final grit used, the water and extraction checks and the result.

procedure: Confirm the test result and the controls from “Pre-work surface assessment and test patches” and “Dust controls: wet methods, extraction, isolation and housekeeping” before the first pass.
Set up the machine, the pads and the water flow, and check the cord and plug.
Start the water, then the machine, and begin with the coarsest grit in the approved sequence.
Check the surface under light between passes, and move to the next grit only when the previous grit's scratches are removed.
Clean the slurry with the wet method and keep the edges wet while working.
Carry out the final polishing step, then inspect the surface under light from several angles.
Record the grit sequence, the water and extraction checks, the inspection result and any defects.

workedExamples.situation: An operator is honing a granite kitchen floor. The coarse pass has left visible scratches, and the operator moves to a finer grit to save time while the scratches are still there.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What should the operator do, and why?
workedExamples.reasoning: A finer grit cannot remove the deeper scratches that the coarser grit left. The result is a surface that looks finished from a distance but still shows the scratches in the light, and the extra passes take more time and material later. The operator returns to the coarser grit until the scratches are removed, then moves to the finer step. The change is recorded on the job record, with the grit used for each pass.

equipmentAndPpe: Honing or polishing machine with a water feed, checked before use
Pads, discs and grit sequence as set by the manufacturer and the test patch
Extraction or on-tool dust control suited to the task (“Dust controls: wet methods, extraction, isolation and housekeeping”)
Light for inspection and a level to check edges where needed
Respiratory protection planned per “Respirators, fit testing and health monitoring” for any residual risk
Eye protection, hearing protection and footwear as set by the site induction

commonErrors.prevention: Move to the next grit only when the previous grit's scratches are removed. Check under light between steps.

commonErrors.error: Running dry to check the surface.
commonErrors.prevention: Keep the wet method running. Check with the surface wet or with the machine stopped and the area still wet.

commonErrors.error: Over-grinding terrazzo until the chips loosen.
commonErrors.prevention: Stop when the matrix and chips are level. Check each chip for looseness and record any loose chips.

commonErrors.error: Using a loaded or damaged pad.
commonErrors.prevention: Clean or replace the pad as the manufacturer directs. A loaded pad scratches the surface.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: The wet method and extraction apply to every honing and polishing step (“Respirable crystalline silica: where it comes from and why it matters” and “Dust controls: wet methods, extraction, isolation and housekeeping”). A dry pass is a stop-work matter.
Check the cord, plug and machine before use.

The grit sequence and machine speed for each job come from the manufacturer and the test patch. This lesson does not set a national standard for the method. Completing this lesson does not grant any licence or certificate for stone restoration.

qualityStandard: The grit sequence is written on the job record before the first pass.
The wet method is running at each grit change and for the whole pass.
The finished surface shows no scratches from the coarser grits, no pits from the work, and no loose chips.
The inspection result and any defects are recorded.
documentationEvidence: Grit and pad sequence used, with machine and speed as set by the manufacturer
Water and extraction check record at start and at each grit change
Inspection record with light conditions and any defects
Defect report for any damage found after the work
summary: Honing comes before polishing, and each grit removes the scratches of the one before.
The wet method runs through every step; dry honing and polishing are not permitted.
Stop over-grinding terrazzo before chips loosen.
Inspect under light from several angles before calling the surface finished.
Record the sequence, checks and inspection result.
referencesAtEnd: Official sources to recheck before any job: NT WorkSafe, Guide to working with crystalline silica and crystalline silica containing products (version 1.1, 29 January 2026); Safe Work Australia, Working with silica and silica containing products (national guidance) (February 2022).

knowledgeChecks.question: Why does honing come before polishing?
options: Honing adds the final shine to the stone surface and the edges of it
Polishing is only for outdoor surfaces like paths and patios on sites
Honing is optional on all jobs of every kind, size and type of stone
Honing levels or removes marks so that polishing can build the sheen

knowledgeChecks.question: What is the rule for moving to a finer grit?
options: Move only when the previous grit's scratches are removed
Move as soon as possible to save time on the job
Move after one minute on every surface type that is treated
Always skip straight to the finest grit available

knowledgeChecks.question: Which method is required throughout honing and polishing in this course?
options: Dry grinding of the whole surface
The wet method at the point of cut
Compressed air to clear the surface
A general-purpose vacuum cleaner

knowledgeChecks.question: Which result is a sign of over-grinding terrazzo?
options: A level matrix and visible chips
An even sheen across the surface
Loosening chips or exposed aggregate
Clean slurry on the edges of the floor

knowledgeChecks.question: Where should the grit sequence and machine speed for a job come from?
options: This course sets them as a national standard for all work
The client's preference only, on the day of the job itself
The regulator issues them for each job separately on request
The manufacturer's instructions and the result of the test patch
